plain_english: With relation whose self is difference-and-non-difference — by whom all things are proved, whose work is world-traffic — him, Śiva, by own will, we praise.
sanskrit_cite: bhedābhedātmasaṃbandhasahasarvārthasādhitā lokayātrā kṛtiryasya svecchayā taṃ stumaḥ śivam

plain_english: Dawning by a body made of relation through being, difference, and the rest — conquering though one: the world-self, light, the supreme Lord.
sanskrit_cite: bhāvabhedādisaṃbandhamayena vapuṣonmiṣan jayatyeko'pi viśvātmā prakāśaḥ parameśvaraḥ

plain_english: Awaiting and dependence are no relation for the two inert ones: impossible — even where selfhood is won, they are metaphor, not definition.
sanskrit_cite: apekṣā pāratantryaṃ ca na saṃbandho jaḍātmanoḥ asaṃbhavādātmalābhe'pyupacāro na lakṣaṇā

plain_english: From the teaching that non-beings obtain selfhood, two-seatedness too is abandoned: form-fusion alone thus stands as relation's meaning.
sanskrit_cite: asatāmātmalābhokterdviṣṭhataivaṃ ca hīyate rūpasaṃśleṣa evaivaṃ saṃbandhārthaḥ sthitaḥ sa ca

plain_english: Not uninterruptedness — for it misses relation: if it were so, it would hold of iron bars. Hence fusion of the many's form — that alone is one-selfhood.
No barring of the many in one's very oneness, others say: things unmixed in themselves — thought joins them.
sanskrit_cite: naikasyaikye'pyanekasya bādha āhuryathā pare ityamiśrāḥ svayaṃ bhāvāstānyojayati kalpanā

plain_english: Since this is no mere thought — it cannot be dismissed: like the snake-error, it resists remedy by clinging to a shining.
Since clinging to a shining is not a thing resembling a shining but a following after shining — error is exactly that: a shining astray.
sanskrit_cite: yasmādābhāsalagnatvaṃ nābhāsasadṛśārthatā kiṃ tvābhāsānusāritvaṃ bhrānta ābhāsa eva tat

plain_english: Thus even in this shining, the many's unity-seeing has a statable warrant — declared plainly in recognition's path.
sanskrit_cite: itthamābhāsa evāsminnanekasyaikatādṛśi vācyopapattiḥ sāpyuktā pratyabhijñānaye sphuṭam
